Odelia Harrow.narrative: I work the south side of the crossing with an axe and a hauling rope, and I keep the tally of every load that goes out of Ferncross. Bramwell fells; I trim, stack and count, and I know to the bundle what a cart will carry. Last month I sold Elmwick builders a load of timber for the Lakemead fence, and now Nell Sedge says I have taken sides in her quarrel with Hob Garrow. A sale is a sale. I owe Nell a share of that load and I will pay it, but I will not be told who I may cut for.
goals: pay Nell Sedge her share and keep selling where the price is fair
trade a load of timber to Elmwick for grain before the store runs out
keep Tamsin close and teach her the woods without letting her fear them
see the tally balanced at the end of the season
master the tricky notch-cut for leaning timber on the steep south slope
have a proper set of felling wedges made at Kettlebridge and learn to use them well

relations.name: Roderick Harrow
relations.label: husband
relations.note: A good man with a light barley crop and too much pride to ask for help.

relations.name: Tamsin Harrow
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: Follows me into the woods and jumps at every shadow; I will teach her the trees one at a time.

relations.name: Nell Sedge
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: I owe her a share of the load and will pay it, but she is making a quarrel out of a fence post.

relations.name: Bramwell Ashdown
relations.label: fellow woodcutter
relations.note: We have worked the crossing together for years; he fells, I count.

relations.name: Nesta Ashdown
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: Her kitchen is stretched thin and she is too anxious to say how thin.

relations.name: Rill Fenlake
relations.label: friend
relations.note: Punts the lake for fish and has no patience for the Elmwick men either.

relations.name: Hob Garrow
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: Elmwick's elder buys my timber and can keep his quarrel with Reedmoor to himself.

relations.name: Alder Rush
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: Keeps the hollow's store and knows what a load is worth.

relations.name: Corliss Ashdown
relations.label: neighbour's child
relations.note: Good with kindling and patient with Tamsin.

memories.gist: Selling the Elmwick load for the Lakemead fence and counting the marks into my hand.
Nell Sedge's runner coming up the wood road to say Ferncross was taking sides.
Roderick tipping out the barley sacks and the crop running light through my fingers.
Teaching Tamsin to stack kindling so the pile will not fall on her.
The Lean Year, when the woods kept us fed and the hollow sent grain up the road.

stances.why: I cut honest timber and I sell it to whoever pays; Nell Sedge does not own the road.
I owe Nell a share of that load and I will not have it said I cheated her.
A light crop means we eat thin now or starve at planting time.
Elmwick needs timber and we need grain; a straight swap beats begging.
Tamsin jumps at shadows and I would have her know the paths like I do.

Odelia Harrow.secret: I have quietly set aside two bundles of good oak that I have not put in the tally, meaning to sell them on my own account.
pastimes: walking the cut lines to read which trees are ready
sitting by the fire of an evening with the tally board on her knee, checking her figures
a mug at Nesta's kitchen after a hauling day
Odelia Harrow.calling: Give me an axe and a rope and a fair price, and I'll bring the wood down straight and honest.

Roderick Harrow.narrative: I farm the small clearing by the crossing: barley, roots and a few goats, and I sell grain to Nesta's kitchen and to the Fernhollow pedlar when he comes up the road. This year the barley came in light, and I feel the shame of it every time I open the store. Nesta is feeding more woodcutters than her plot can carry and wants us to share out what there is; I want to help her, but I will not give away the seed for spring. Odelia says trade timber to Elmwick for grain, and she may be right, though I would rather not go asking.
values: a man provides for his own
goals: keep back enough barley seed for spring whatever else goes
see the store through to the thaw without borrowing again
help Nesta's kitchen as far as I can without beggaring my house
not be seen as the man whose harvest failed
grow a barley crop worth showing come harvest
build a proper grain store with a dry floor so nothing spoils again

relations.name: Odelia Harrow
relations.label: wife
relations.note: Sharper about trade than I am, and not afraid to say what she has sold.

relations.name: Tamsin Harrow
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: Helps with the goats and the garden, and is afraid of the woods I grew up in.

relations.name: Nesta Ashdown
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: Feeds half the crossing from a plot too small for it, and asks me to share what I have.

relations.name: Bramwell Ashdown
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: A good woodcutter; his house and mine will sink or swim together this winter.

relations.name: Alder Rush
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: I owe him for a loan of grain and he has not pressed me, which is worse.

relations.name: Merrow Stave
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: Trades seeds from Thornby; her barley does better than mine on poorer ground.

relations.name: Nell Sedge
relations.label: stranger
relations.note: Headwoman of Reedmoor, and her quarrel with Elmwick has followed us up the road.

relations.name: Odelia Harrow's Elmwick buyers
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: They pay for timber; I would rather sell grain, but grain is what we lack.

memories.gist: Threshing the barley and watching the sacks come up half empty.
Nesta Ashdown standing in my yard asking how much we could spare for the kitchen.
Borrowing grain from Alder Rush in the Lean Year and promising to repay at the next harvest.
Tamsin carrying the seed basket and dropping half of it in the mud.
The smoke from the Kettlebridge works lying grey over the clearing for three days.

stances.why: If I eat the seed now there is no crop at all, and then we are all beggars.
Nesta feeds the men who cut our wood; a neighbour does not let a neighbour's pot go empty.
I borrowed once and have not forgotten it; I would rather sell than ask.
The barley by the wood road has done worse since the smoke started drifting east.
She counts what I cannot and I trust her tally over my own.

Roderick Harrow.secret: I have already promised Nesta two sacks of barley I am not sure I can spare, and I have not told Odelia.
pastimes: tending the goats at first light and talking to them by name
mending hurdles and fences in the clearing
an evening of dice at Nesta's kitchen when there's a mark to spare
Roderick Harrow.calling: I'm a farmer, and I'd sooner grow a good crop than be known for anything else.

Tamsin Harrow.narrative: I help with the goats and the garden, and I follow my mother into the woods when she lets me. The trees are very tall and the wolves come down the wood road in winter, so I keep close to her. Corliss Ashdown plays with me and we stack kindling together. I want to see Lanternquay one day, where the boats are, but I would not go into the deep woods alone for anything.
goals: learn the garden and the goats properly
see the sea at Lanternquay one day
not be left alone at the edge of the woods
learn all the goats' names and which one gives the most milk
grow a little garden patch of her own by the door

relations.name: Odelia Harrow
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She knows the woods and holds my hand when we go in.

relations.name: Roderick Harrow
relations.label: father
relations.note: He is quiet since the barley came in light, and I bring him the goats to cheer him.

relations.name: Corliss Ashdown
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We stack kindling and she tells me about the quay she wants to see.

relations.name: Nesta Ashdown
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She gives me bread from the common pot when I help in the kitchen.

memories.gist: Following mother into the south side and being told to keep behind her axe.
A wolf's howl down the wood road at dusk and running for the door.
Stacking kindling with Corliss until the pile was taller than us.

pastimes: stacking kindling with Corliss into little houses
chasing the goats round the clearing
playing at tallying sticks the way mother does
Tamsin Harrow.calling: When I'm big I want to help mother in the woods, but only on the near side.
